insights.insight: The protocol has produced 9,743 cryptographically verified purchase receipts — each one a confirmed transaction, not an inferred intent. In a post-cookie environment where $5+ CPM buys a probabilistic guess, a verified receipt is a categorically different asset.

The April 9 record cycle added $56,064 in GMV from only 42 receipts — roughly $1,335 per receipt — indicating the network is capturing high-basket, high-intent buyers, not just frequent small-ticket transactions.
The 7-day GMV window reached $208,920 as of April 10, up from $101,734 one week prior — a doubling of weekly velocity that suggests the signal pool is compounding, not plateauing.

insights.topic: Geographic reach now spans 16 CBSAs including major DMAs
insights.insight: Confirmed metros include NYC, LA, Philadelphia, Boston, Seattle, Miami, Tampa, and Pittsburgh, with non-metro coverage in WA, OK, AL, ID, MI, RI, MA, and DC — a footprint that supports national campaign planning, not just pilot markets.

insights.topic: Category entropy signals cross-vertical targeting potential
insights.insight: At 3.262 bits of category entropy, no single retail vertical dominates the receipt pool — grocery, home improvement, electronics, restaurant, and now SaaS-subscription coexist, meaning the dataset can support targeting briefs across multiple brand categories.

April 9 marked the first non-physical-commerce category in the protocol's history, opening the signal set beyond brick-and-mortar retail to digital subscription buyers — a distinct and historically hard-to-verify audience segment.
